newsitem.title: UK: GRAND NATIONAL RACE ABANDONED AFTER BOMB SCARES.
newsitem.headline: GRAND NATIONAL RACE ABANDONED AFTER BOMB SCARES.

text.p: The Grand National horse race, one of Britain's greatest sporting events, had to be abandoned on Saturday because of a bomb alert which prompted total evacuation of the race course.
Police told officials at Aintree course, near the north-west city of Liverpool, to clear the site after receiving coded warnings of two bombs on the site.

"The police have received two coded bomb warnings, and they felt it was the most appropriate thing to evacuate the entire racecourse," Aintree spokesman Nigel Payne told reporters. "From our point of view, the safety of spectators is the most paramount thing."
Some 60,000 spectators plus the 38 jockeys were moved off the site some 30 minutes before the 1445 GMT scheduled start of the race.
Officials said later they had decided to abandon racing for the rest of the day.

The bomb alert at the world's most famous steeplechases followed massive disruption on motorways in central England on Thursday after the discovery of two Irish Republican Army (IRA) bombs on road bridges.
It was not immediately clear who had delivered the bomb warnings at the Aintree course or whether any devices were actually left on the site.
Jockey Carl Llewellyn, due to ride Camelot King in the big race, described the situation as sick. "Whoever did this are not sportsmen," he said.
Jenny Pitman, trainer of such past winners as Corbieres and Royal Athlete, called for the horses to be returned to the starting gate and the race to be run.
"We cannot be held to ransom and give in to these people. We have the lunatic element here. We can't give in to them," she said.

Helicopters hovered overhead while police, fire and ambulance crews stood by. Armed policed had been in evidence over the three days of the race meeting as a precautionary measure but until Saturday there had been no full-scale alert.
Four years ago the Grand National ended in turmoil in different circumstances after two false starts led to the race being declared void.

The IRA has been campaigning for more than 25 years for an end to British rule of Northern Ireland. It called off a 17-month long ceasefire in February last year and has since exploded several large bombs on the British mainland.
Security sources believe the IRA is trying to force Northern Ireland on to the political agenda of the British May 1 election campaign, where it has received scant attention.

IRA strategy for years has been to attack the British mainland to force British public opinion to put pressure on the government to find a solution to the 28-year Northern Ireland conflict, which has cost billions of dollars and 3,200 lives.
